title: Handoff Quickledger: 03/11-03/12
content:
Quickledger — informal on-call handoff notes (use as scratchpad).

Shift window: 2026-03-11 19:00 -> 2026-03-12 07:00 PST
Taken by: Ethan M. (phone: +1-415-555-0191)
Next: Priya S. (primary), Liam O. (backup)

TL;DR:
- Major: brief latency spike 03/12 01:14 across hosted_api-east-1 (p95 went from 120ms -> 700ms for ~12m).
- Temporary mitigation applied: auto-fallback to smaller model shard (gptx-mini-1) for burst routing; reduced p95 back to ~160ms.
- Ongoing: one routing pool (pool-7-gpu-a) showing memory fragmentation after repeated quantized model loads. Recreate pod on next maintenance window.

Active alerts (what to watch right away):
1) alert: CPUThrottling_high_pool-7 — firing since 2026-03-12 00:58 — symptom: sustained kernel CPU steal on node-a3-07 -> causes slow scheduling and queuing.
   - Quick check: kubectl top node node-a3-07; dmesg | tail; ssh to node and check nvidia-smi.
   - Temporary action taken: cordoned node-a3-07 and drained non-critical pods (left serving-runtime pods on): kubectl drain node-a3-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data (did with caution).
   - Impact: slight capacity reduction; autoscaler picked up a replacement but new node not fully warmed (time to spin ~4m).

2) alert: ModelKVCache_evictions_high on redwood-cache-prod (firing intermittently)
   - Observed ~20% increase in cache misses during spike. Suspect pattern: many short requests followed by long-gen fallbacks -> KV churn.
   - Mitigation: enabled prefix caching for route /api/v1/generate/low-latency-temp (quick config change in Console -> routing -> prefixCache=true). Rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Currently at 50% as of 01:32.
   - Note: Check memory pressure on cache hosts after full rollout.

Incident timeline (brief):
- 01:12: first small latency jitter reported by RUM telemetry for hosted_api-east-1 (p50 stable, p95 rising).
- 01:14: Alert fired (p95 > 500ms).
- 01:16: Correlated with node-a3-07 CPU steal, multiple pods stuck in ContainerCreating due to cached driver conflict during auto-update.
- 01:19: Cordoned node, drained non-critical pods; traffic rebalanced -> p95 improved.
- 01:24: Applied auto-fallback routing policy to smaller model variant for low-cost tier; observed p95 ~160ms.
- 01:40: Asked infra team to schedule a manual reboot for node-a3-07; created JIRA/INFR-4123 to track.

Commands used (copypaste safe):
- kubectl get pods -n serving --field-selector=status.phase!=Running
- kubectl describe pod <pod> -n serving | sed -n '1,120p'
- kubectl drain node-a3-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- curl -s -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>' -d '{"route":"/api/v1/generate/low-latency-temp","fallback_model":"gptx-mini-1","percent":50}' https://console.api.redwood.internal/routing/update
- ssh root@node-a3-07 'journalctl -u docker -n 200'

Temporary runbook steps (for next shift — keep until infra fully remediates):
1) If p95 > 400ms in hosted_api-east-1 for >5m:
   - Confirm which nodes report high steal: kubectl top nodes | sort -k3 -nr
   - If a specific node shows >30% steal consistently, cordon and drain low-priority pools.
   - Enable auto-fallback route to gptx-mini-1 at 50% traffic first, then 100% if no improvement in 3m.
2) If ModelKVCache_evictions_high persists after prefixCache rollout to 100%:
   - Temporarily increase cache shard memory by +12% via infra-config (only do during low-traffic window unless agreed with infra).
   - If memory increase not possible, add route-based aggressive TTL for transient keys: setTTL(route, 30s).
3) If new pods stuck in ContainerCreating frequently after AMI/driver updates:
   - Check node labels for 'driver-update-pending'. If present, avoid scheduling critical pods onto those nodes.
   - Open infra ticket and request node remediation or rollback.

Known quirks (carry-forward notes):
- Serving runtime kernel v2.14 behaves poorly with mixed quantized and fp16 loads on same node (observed OOM-like thrashing). Prefer node pool 'quant-pool' for quantized-only models.
- Console routing UI shows stale percent values until cache cleared; use API for immediate changes.
- When rolling back a model, remember to clear per-route KV cache for that model-id to avoid serving stale hidden-state combos (command: curl POST /internal/cache/clear?model_id=...).

Sticky TODOs (not urgent but helpful):
- Recreate pool-7-gpu-a pod image with pinned nvidia driver 525.85 (temp fix) — PR open: runtime#889 (needs review).
- Add a short eval to verify quality regression when switching to gptx-mini-1 for fallback routes (owner: Priya). Blocker: none, but add sample prompts to /evals/fallback-quality/mini-1.json.
- Update on-call runbook to include the exact api call for prefixCache toggle (owner: Ethan).

Contacts & escalation (quick):
- Infra (node/AMI/driver): oncall-infra -> #infra-pagers (Slack) / pagerduty: INFRA-OPS
- Serving runtime leads: Priya Srinivasan (Slack @priya) / pagerduty: SERV-LEAD
- Platform Eng (autoscaler): Liam O'Connor / slack @liam / escalate to platform-ops if autoscaler doesn't produce replacement within 6m

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did autoscaler spin a replacement but it took ~4m to become warm? Investigate boot image or warm pool shortage.
- Should we add a warm standby of quant-pool nodes in east-1? Cost tradeoffs to discuss with infra.
- Validate whether prefixCache at 100% increases cost materially for top customers (tag: billing-impact).

Handy notes for next shift (one-liners):
- If you need to roll back routing percent quickly, use the Console API with a 3s timeout and check route-status immediately after change.
- When cordoning nodes, prefer drain flags that keep serving-runtime running (we drained low-priority first to avoid double-eviction).
- Keep an eye on real-user-monitoring (RUM) p95 and synthetic probe locations (east-1, west-2).

End of quickledger. Re-use or trim as needed; this is intended as a "scratch-handoff" rather than canonical runbook.

-- Ethan
